message.content:
Let me look at the git history of the gdatetime.c file to understand the fix for this specific issue. Let me check the actual bug. The issue is a global-buffer-overflow READ 2. Let me think about where a global buffer is read.

The `days_in_months` array is a global. Let me check `g_date_time_new`:
```c
  if (year < 1 || year > 9999 ||
      month < 1 || month > 12 ||
      day < 1 || day > days_in_months[GREGORIAN_LEAP (year)][month] ||
```

Here `days_in_months[GREGORIAN_LEAP(year)][month]`. If `month` is out of range... but month is checked `month < 1 || month > 12` first. But wait, `GREGORIAN_LEAP(year)` - if year is out of range? year is checked `year < 1 || year > 9999`. Hmm.

Actually wait - the `||` short-circuits. `month < 1 || month > 12` is checked before `days_in_months[...][month]`. So month is in [1,12]. And `GREGORIAN_LEAP(year)` returns 0 or 1. So `days_in_months[0 or 1][1..12]` is fine.

Let me look at `days_in_months` definition.
